articles.title: 'SOMEONE SAVE AMERICA': Huge Uproar In US Congress Amid Iran War; Trump Blasted Over Prices

Her remarks add to a growing debate in Congress over the economic impact of the war, including concerns about costs facing families across the United States.

articles.title: Jharkhand exam cancellations leave appointed candidates in limbo after govt cancels 22, probes 23
articles.description: Jharkhand's government cancelled twenty-two recruitment examinations and ordered investigations into twenty-three others. This decision followed a twenty-six-day student protest concerning alleged recruitment irregularities. Successful candidates who had already joined government departments expressed their deep disappointment and concern. The government aims to restore confidence in the recruitment system following widespread allegations of malpractice. Investigations have intensified with several arrests made in connection with the alleged recruitment irregularities.

articles.title: India's Voter ID: Sergio Gor Backs Trump On India’s Voter ID; Congress Hits Back On EVM, S.I.R
articles.description: A political face-off has erupted after U.S. President Donald Trump praised India’s voter ID system and called for a similar requirement in the United States. U.S. Ambassador to India Sergio Gor backed Trump’s position, saying voter ID is essential and said the United States should adopt a similar requirement when people vote. Gor highlighted India’s large electorate and low share of postal voting while calling voter ID a non-partisan issue. Congress spokesperson Pawan Khera hit back with a sarcastic response, challenging the U.S. to adopt India’s electoral practices, including EVMs and S.I.R. Khera also took a swipe at Trump’s comments on voter identification. The exchange comes amid an intensifying debate in the U.S. over election reforms, voter ID requirements and electoral integrity, with India’s voting system now at the centre of the political conversation.

articles.title: Jharkhand Student Protest: Agitation Continues for 26th Day in Ranchi
articles.description: Student protests in Ranchi, Jharkhand have entered their 26th day, with students continuing to demand a CBI probe into alleged examination irregularities. Meanwhile, the state government has issued a notification announcing several measures, including the cancellation of the JSSC CGL examination and other exams conducted by TDPL. The government has also ordered a CID investigation into alleged examination irregularities since 2014 and announced internal monitoring mechanisms for JPSC and JSSC. To improve the examination system, a committee headed by IAS officer Amitabh Kaushal will be formed. The government will also request the High Court to establish fast-track courts for quicker disposal of cases related to examination fraud. However, the controversy has deepened after candidates who secured government jobs through the CGL examination protested against its cancellation. They argue that they followed the legal recruitment process and that cancelling the examination suddenly could affect around 2,000 families. They accuse the government of giving in to crowd pressure and demand that the cancellation decision be withdrawn.

articles.title: Bihar Student Protest: Tejashwi Yadav to Lead Raj Bhavan March
articles.description: The student movement in Bihar has intensified over demands for reforms in the examination system, unemployment, recruitment irregularities, and alleged paper leaks. Students are protesting at Gardanibagh in Patna, while political activity around the issue is also gaining momentum. RJD leader and Bihar’s Leader of Opposition Tejashwi Yadav is scheduled to lead a Raj Bhavan march from JP Golambar in Gandhi Maidan. He has accused the Bihar government of ignoring students’ concerns and failing to address issues related to recruitment and examination irregularities. Tejashwi also plans to protest against alleged AK-47 firing during the students’ agitation. The BJP, however, has criticized him, calling his politics “part-time” and accusing him of appearing only to gain political visibility. BJP leaders argue that the students’ issues have already been addressed, with examinations and results completed, and therefore question the continuation of the protest.
